races.paceDynamic: Ramon Di Loria is the only confirmed front runner in this field and will dictate terms from the start, likely setting a sustainable pace without pressure from other early types. Rain Cap may provide some early company as a prominent runner, but the lack of genuine pace pressure means Ramon Di Loria can control the tempo and kick clear when asked. With seven hold-up horses relying on a strong pace to set up their finishing kicks, the likely modest gallop will severely compromise their chances. This race shape strongly favours front runners and prominent racers who can avoid the inevitable traffic problems behind.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Uncontested Front Runner Dominance
scenarios.trigger: If Ramon Di Loria gets an easy lead and kicks clear turning for home
scenarios.body: The lack of early pace allows him to dictate ideal fractions and have plenty left for a decisive move. The hold-up brigade get caught in traffic as the pace quickens late, unable to make up the ground.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Clear Away
scenarios.trigger: If Ramon Di Loria and Rain Cap work together early then battle clear
scenarios.body: These two get first run on the field while the seven hold-up horses are still organising behind them. The tactical advantage of racing handy proves decisive in a slowly-run affair.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Traffic Chaos Favours Lucky
scenarios.trigger: If the large pack of hold-up horses creates a cavalry charge finish
scenarios.body: The bunched field creates interference and only the horses getting clear runs can capitalise. Rambuso Creek and Invincible Ruby have the class edge if finding daylight.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Surprise Speed From Behind
scenarios.trigger: If one of the hold-up horses gets an unusually strong pace to aim at
scenarios.body: Despite the tactical disadvantage, superior finishing speed from Sunlit Sea or Rambuso Creek could still prevail. This requires Ramon Di Loria to go too fast early or the field to spread out unusually.

races.paceDynamic: With no confirmed front runner among nine hold-up horses, this race will see a cautious early gallop as runners settle behind each other waiting for someone to take responsibility. The likely scenario is a slow crawl through the early stages before building into a sprint finish over the final 2-3 furlongs. Howzak and Great Success may find forward positions by default, but neither is a natural pace-setter, creating a muddling tempo that will suit horses with a sharp turn of foot. This tactical setup strongly favours hold-up horses who can produce their best work late, particularly those with proven sprint finishes at this distance.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Slow Burn Sprint Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is crawling early and builds into a cavalry charge
scenarios.body: The lack of natural pace-setters creates a stop-start gallop that becomes a 2-furlong dash. Sharp finishers like Maynora and Howzak can exploit their sprint speed from off the pace.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Steadier Even Gallop
scenarios.trigger: If one or two horses commit to making the running
scenarios.body: A more honest tempo suits horses who can travel well and sustain their effort. This brings Great Success and April Diamond into calculations with their proven staying power at the trip.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: False Pace Collapse
scenarios.trigger: If early leaders set unsustainable fractions then fade
scenarios.body: Horses tracking the pace suffer when leaders capitulate, allowing backmarkers to sweep through. Stormy Pearl and Belling The Cat benefit from being held up furthest off the early speed.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Tactical Stalemate
scenarios.trigger: If jockeys are too patient and leave it impossibly late
scenarios.body: Over-cautious riding leaves all runners with too much to do in the final furlong. The most experienced campaigner Howzak uses his racecraft to edge a messy finish.

Howzak is returning from 101-day absence and may need the run despite his fresh form record.
Track any early pace development as runners sort themselves out in the opening two furlongs.
Monitor Stormy Pearl for market confidence given David Thompson's modest recent strike rate.

races.paceDynamic: So Alex will take them along from the front with minimal early pressure, as Dance Time, Marbuzet and Trojan Sun are the only other prominent runners but lack the pace to challenge early. The large field of hold-up horses including Gentle Warrior, Ouro Preto, Banderas and Torcello will settle behind, creating a steady gallop through the first mile. This sets up a classic staying test where the pace will quicken from 3f out as the hold-up brigade fan wide looking for racing room. This race shape strongly favours hold-up horses who can produce a sustained finish, as the uncontested early pace will leave plenty in reserve for the closing stages.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If So Alex sets uncontested fractions and the pace stays steady through the first mile
scenarios.body: The large contingent of closers get perfect conditions to unleash finishing kicks, with the early leader vulnerable to multiple challengers in the final 2f. The soft ground will aid stamina-laden finishers who can grind past tiring pace-setters.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runners Hold On
scenarios.trigger: If So Alex gets an easy lead and Dance Time or Marbuzet apply just enough pressure to keep honest fractions
scenarios.body: The modest early pace leaves the leaders with enough left to resist late challenges, particularly if the hold-up horses get caught in traffic or are too far back. Prominent racers benefit from the tactical advantage of racing handy.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Mid-Race Injection Changes Dynamic
scenarios.trigger: If Dance Time or Trojan Sun decide to take the race to So Alex earlier than expected around the back straight
scenarios.body: A faster middle section stretches the field and exposes any fitness doubts, potentially setting up the race for horses who can sit closer and have a shorter sprint finish. This favours the better-rated closers with tactical speed.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Completely
scenarios.trigger: If So Alex goes too slowly and multiple horses start making moves turning for home
scenarios.body: A messy, stop-start affair develops where positioning becomes crucial and the first horse to get a clear run wins. This chaotic finish could suit any horse with a clean passage regardless of running style.

watchPoints.text: So Alex could get an uncontested lead that proves impossible to peg back if the hold-up horses are too far behind

Torcello at 12 years old represents great value if the pace sets up right for his proven staying ability

races.paceDynamic: Hostility and Bellasio are the only confirmed early pace horses in a field dominated by hold-up runners, creating a pedestrian gallop from the outset. With just two prominent runners against ten hold-up types, the pace will be moderate to slow, allowing the leaders to conserve energy for the business end. This race shape heavily favours prominent runners who can dictate terms without pressure, as the hold-up brigade will face a wall of horses and limited room for manoeuvre in the straight. The early pace advantage is decisive here - prominent runners should dominate.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent runners dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Hostility and Bellasio are allowed to bowl along unchallenged in front
scenarios.body: The lack of early pace pressure allows them to quicken when it matters while the hold-up horses get caught in traffic. The two pace-setters have first run on the field when the sprint develops.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-up horse finds clear run
scenarios.trigger: If one of the better hold-up horses gets a dream passage through
scenarios.body: Union Island or Soames Forsyte could capitalise on their class edge if avoiding the inevitable traffic problems. The moderate pace helps their finishing kick but they need serious luck in running.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Surprise from back markers
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses completely and becomes a sprint from the 2f pole
scenarios.body: Age Of Time and Jkr Cobbler could exploit their light weights in a cavalry charge finish. Their class disadvantage is negated by the scramble but they need everything to fall right.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Tactical mess benefits outsider
scenarios.trigger: If the front two go too slow then suddenly sprint clear unexpectedly
scenarios.body: The hold-up horses are caught flat-footed by the sudden injection of pace from the leaders. An each-way outsider like Gainsbourg could sneak through while others are still organising their challenges.

races.paceDynamic: Sandy Craic and Velvet Rhythm will set the early tempo from the front, with Blufferonthebus likely tracking just behind in the prominent positions. The pace should be sustainable rather than fierce given the small field size and lack of multiple confirmed front-runners. From the 3f pole, the hold-up horses like Pickersgill, Amelia's Joy and Sailor's Return will be unleashed from off the pace. This race shape strongly favours hold-up horses who can finish fast, as the early pace will be moderate and create opportunities for closers to pick off the leaders.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is moderate as expected with Sandy Craic and Velvet Rhythm setting sustainable fractions
scenarios.body: The closers will have too much firepower late and sweep past the early leaders in the final furlong. Pickersgill's recent 7f win and Amelia's Joy's hold-up style perfectly suit this development.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runners Steal It
scenarios.trigger: If Sandy Craic or Velvet Rhythm gets away with soft fractions and kicks clear turning for home
scenarios.body: One of the pace-setters will have enough left to hold off the late challenge from the closers. Velvet Rhythm's recent 7f wins show she can sustain her speed over this trip.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Blufferonthebus gets the perfect trip tracking the leaders and avoids the early pace battle
scenarios.body: She can slip through on the rail or find clear running to outfinish both the pace-setters and late closers. Her recent second over 8f on soft ground is encouraging.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Surprise Package
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses completely and becomes a sprint finish where early position matters
scenarios.body: Anorah Unleashed's light weight and unknown quantity factor could see her spring a shock if getting a dream run. The 7lb claimer takes a valuable chunk off her back.

races.paceDynamic: The Gay Blade and Good Karma will take the field along at a steady but not punishing gallop through the soft ground over this 7f trip. With six hold-up horses in the field, there's minimal early pressure on the pace-setters, allowing them to dictate comfortable fractions. The large contingent of hold-up performers will be bunched towards the rear, creating potential traffic problems and leaving them reliant on splits opening in the straight. This race shape strongly favours the prominent racers and those with tactical pace who can avoid the inevitable scramble from the back.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Runners Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If The Gay Blade and Good Karma maintain their positions without serious pressure
scenarios.body: The pace-setters control the tempo and have first run on the field, while the hold-up brigade gets caught in traffic behind them. The tactical advantage of racing handy proves decisive on soft ground where late momentum is harder to generate.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Find Gaps
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes genuinely strong or traffic problems don't materialize for the back markers
scenarios.body: Saisons d'Or and Jamaican Storm get clear runs through and benefit from the strong gallop, with their proven ability at this trip coming to the fore. The soft conditions suit their grinding style once they find daylight.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Early
scenarios.trigger: If The Gay Blade and Good Karma go too fast early on the testing ground
scenarios.body: The leaders weaken dramatically in the final furlong, allowing the hold-up horses with the best finishing kicks to sweep past. King Sharja and El Pinto emerge from the pack with strong late runs.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Tactical Speed Wins
scenarios.trigger: If one horse can secure an ideal stalking position just behind the leaders
scenarios.body: A horse tracking the pace gets the perfect trip and kicks clear when the leaders tire but before the hold-up horses can organize their challenges. This requires perfect positioning and timing from jockey and horse.
